stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of coronary heart disease?
rationale: Atherosclerosis causes cerebrovascular, coronary, and peripheral vascular disease.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of peripheral vascular disease?
rationale: Atherosclerosis causes cerebrovascular, coronary, and peripheral vascular disease.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: Cholesterol synthesis requires which substance?
rationale: Cholesterol is synthesized from acetyl-CoA by a lengthy pathway that may be divided into five steps.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS BIOSYNTHESIZED FROM ACETYL-CoA > Acetyl-CoA Is the Source of All Carbon Atoms in Cholesterol

stem: Mevalonate phosphorylation requires which substance?
rationale: Mevalonate is phosphorylated sequentially using ATP by three kinases.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS BIOSYNTHESIZED FROM ACETYL-CoA > Acetyl-CoA Is the Source of All Carbon Atoms in Cholesterol

stem: Farnesyl diphosphate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Dolichol and ubiquinone are polyisoprenoids formed from farnesyl diphosphate by the addition of isopentenyl diphosphate residues.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS BIOSYNTHESIZED FROM ACETYL-CoA > Farnesyl Diphosphate Gives Rise to Dolichol & Ubiquinone

stem: Which substance is stored in the endoplasmic reticulum?
rationale: Squalene epoxidase is a mixed-function oxidase in the endoplasmic reticulum.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS BIOSYNTHESIZED FROM ACETYL-CoA > Acetyl-CoA Is the Source of All Carbon Atoms in Cholesterol

stem: Oxidosqualene-lanosterol cyclase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Cyclization is catalyzed by oxidosqualene-lanosterol cyclase.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS BIOSYNTHESIZED FROM ACETYL-CoA > Acetyl-CoA Is the Source of All Carbon Atoms in Cholesterol

stem: Which substance is transported by cholesterol?
rationale: Cholesterol is transported in plasma in lipoproteins.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS TRANSPORTED BETWEEN TISSUES IN PLASMA LIPOPROTEINS

stem: Which substance is synthesised by the intestine?
rationale: Cholesterol synthesized in the intestines is incorporated into chylomicrons.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS TRANSPORTED BETWEEN TISSUES IN PLASMA LIPOPROTEINS

stem: Which substance is transported by the liver?
rationale: Most of the cholesterol secreted by the liver in very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) is retained during the formation of intermediate-density lipoprotein (IDL) and ultimately LDL.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS TRANSPORTED BETWEEN TISSUES IN PLASMA LIPOPROTEINS

stem: In which structure is the LDL receptor found?
rationale: LDL is taken up by the LDL receptor in liver and extrahepatic tissues.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS TRANSPORTED BETWEEN TISSUES IN PLASMA LIPOPROTEINS

stem: In which structure is cholesteryl ester found?
rationale: In humans, much of the cholesteryl ester carried in lipoproteins is delivered to the liver via VLDL remnants (IDL) or LDL.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS TRANSPORTED BETWEEN TISSUES IN PLASMA LIPOPROTEINS > Cholesteryl Ester Transfer Protein Facilitates Transfer of Cholesteryl Ester From HDL to Other Lipoproteins

stem: Which substance is synthesised by the liver?
rationale: Cholesterol is excreted from the body via the bile either in the unesterified form or after conversion into bile acids in the liver.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS

stem: Which substrate does cholesterol 7α-hydroxylase act on?
rationale: The principal rate-limiting step in the biosynthesis of bile acids is at the CYP7A1 reaction.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Bile Acid Synthesis Is Regulated at the CYP7A1 Step

stem: Which substance is required by cholesterol 7α-hydroxylase?
rationale: CYP7A1 requires oxygen, NADPH, and cytochrome P450.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Bile Acids Are Formed From Cholesterol

stem: Anions are converted into which substance?
rationale: The anions of the glyco- or tauro- conjugates are termed bile salts.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Bile Acids Are Formed From Cholesterol

stem: In which structure are bile acids found?
rationale: The pool of bile acids, about 3-5 grams, is cycled through the intestine 6 to 10 times each day.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Most Bile Acids Return to the Liver in the Enterohepatic Circulation

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of atherosclerosis?
rationale: Atherosclerosis is an inflammatory disease characterized by the deposition of cholesterol and cholesteryl ester from the plasma lipoproteins into the artery wall.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Serum Cholesterol Is Correlated With the Incidence of Atherosclerosis & Coronary Heart Disease

stem: Plasma cholesterol excess is a risk factor for which condition?
rationale: Elevated plasma cholesterol levels greater than 5mmol/L are one of the most important factors in promoting atherosclerosis.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Serum Cholesterol Is Correlated With the Incidence of Atherosclerosis & Coronary Heart Disease

stem: In which structure is very-low-density lipoprotein found?
rationale: Smaller VLDL particles are utilized by extrahepatic tissues at a slower rate than larger particles, which is considered atherogenic.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Diet and Lifestyle Can Play an Important Role in Reducing Serum Cholesterol

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hypercholesterolemia?
rationale: The defect in familial hypercholesterolemia is most often in the gene for the LDL receptor. LDL is not cleared from the blood in familial hypercholesterolemia.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview > CHOLESTEROL IS EXCRETED FROM THE BODY IN THE BILE AS CHOLESTEROL OR AS BILE ACIDS > Primary Disorders of the Plasma Lipoproteins (Dyslipoproteinemias) Are Inherited

stem: What is the substrate that HMG-CoA reductase acts on?
rationale: Initially, mevalonate is synthesized from acetyl-CoA via a reaction catalyzed by HMG-CoA reductase, which regulated the entire pathway.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview

stem: A five-carbon isoprenoid unit is converted into which substance?
rationale: Next, a five-carbon isoprenoid unit is formed, and six of these condense to form squalene. Squalene undergoes cyclization to form the parent steroid lanosterol, which, after the loss of three methyl groups and other changes, forms cholesterol.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview

stem: Squalene is converted into which substance?
rationale: Squalene undergoes cyclization to form the parent steroid lanosterol, which, after the loss of three methyl groups and other changes, forms cholesterol.
citation: chapter_26_cholesterol_synthesis_transport_and_excretion — Overview
